title: Examining Convergence of Cluster Perturbation Theory and Cluster Coupled Cluster for J1-J2 Heisenberg Spin Lattices
abstract: In previous work, it was shown that using the cluster mean field(cMF) wavefunction as the zeroth order wavefunction for perturbation theory and coupled cluster produces a reasonable approximation for the J 1-J 2 Heisenberg model in the thermodynamic limit(TDL). However, this work was limited to cPT4 and cCCSD. The central claim of cMF is that it takes strongly correlated systems and makes them weakly correlated so that PT weakly correlated methods can be used. To confirm that this claim is true, it is important to show that the PT and CC series converge. In this paper, we extend the previous calculations to cPT7 and cCCSDTQ5 where we show that the energy is converging. We also discuss how to perform cluster based calculations efficiently in the thermodynamic limit, which is crucial for these more expensive calculations.
summary: This paper investigates the convergence of Cluster Perturbation Theory and Coupled Cluster methods when applied to the $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg Spin Lattice. By extending calculations to high orders, the authors confirm that both theoretical series converge, yielding robust predictions for the system's energy and magnetic phase boundaries. This validates the use of these advanced quantum many-body techniques for strongly correlated magnetic materials.
main_problem: The central goal is to rigorously confirm the convergence of high-order Perturbation Theory (PT) and Coupled Cluster (CC) series when applied to strongly correlated quantum spin systems.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that both the PT and CC series converge at high orders (up to cPT7 and cCCSDTQ5), providing reliable estimates for the energy and critical points of the model.
method: The study employs advanced many-body quantum chemistry techniques, specifically Cluster Perturbation Theory and Cluster Coupled Cluster methods, adapted for lattice Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The system studied is the $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg Spin Lattice, described by a Hamiltonian involving nearest-neighbor ($J_1$) and next-nearest-neighbor ($J_2$) exchange interactions between spins.
key_observables: Energy per site, magnetization ($\langle S_i^z angle$), and the critical point position as a function of the ratio $J_2/J_1$.
important_parameters: The ratio of coupling constants $J_2/J_1$, and the calculation is performed in the Thermodynamic Limit (TDL).
main_assumptions: The methods rely on the cluster mean-field (cMF) wavefunction as a zeroth-order approximation, and the calculations utilize approximations inherent to the CC formalism for the TDL.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy per site and magnetization across different ground state regimes (Néel, paramagnetic, collinear) for both PT and CC results, and show the convergence of the critical point estimate.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework by extending calculations to higher orders (cPT7, cCCSDTQ5). It then presents the convergence analysis for energy and magnetization across various $J_2/J_1$ ratios, comparing the results from PT and CC methods.
why_interesting: The rigorous testing of convergence for high-order many-body methods like CC and PT is crucial for developing reliable theoretical tools to predict phase transitions and ground states in complex magnetic materials.
